name: Pullman estate (1800 S. Calumet Avenue): the two-storey brick lodge between the glasshouse ranges

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters it 'D', a dwelling, at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges; the sheet-28 census reads it as the estate's gardener's lodge (s28-pullman-garden-lodge, tier reconstructed): nothing names its occupant or use beyond the 1911 'D'.

research_note: T-3164 (piece 1 of T-1934): built on the district draft's builder (generators/archetypes/prairie_draft.py) because no kit carries a small service dwelling yet, and exempt from the draft rules' re-derivation because the rules' skip names it (as T-2538 did for 1801). Read off sheet 28 by hand: the colour trace would follow this copy's pink wash, which runs diagonally into the east glasshouse range rather than stopping at the lodge's dashed east line. Heights, roof and openings are the draft rules' brick-family values (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). T-3165 refines it to the pictures.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the sheet-28 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json, allocation s28-pullman-service-garden) rules the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground and its lodge present in 1904. Its building date, which the census reads off the 1894 conservatory plate, is T-3165's to read from the pictures themselves.

position.symbolic_location: 1800 S. Calumet Avenue, parcel calumet_1800 (data/street_grid/1904.json): the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground across 18th Street from the house, west side of Calumet Avenue between 18th and 20th Streets; the two-storey building at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges.
position.note: The north-east corner, read off the committed sheet 28 raster at pixel (3186, 2359) where the drawn wall lines cross, and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json; 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses): local E 1470.53, N -3274.69. The bearing turns the plan onto the sheet's own ruled lines (1.014 degrees off east in that fit), so u runs west to the alley and v south, and the building runs square to the lot as drawn.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is the pixel named in the note, of the committed sheet 28 raster, carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: u from the east wall west to the alley, v from the north wall south. The drawn lines' centres on the sheet (x 3009-3186, y 2359-2588) at 0.0506 m a pixel: 8.95 by 11.58 m. Its north wall is the north range's south end and its east wall the east range's west end, as the sheet draws them.

stories.note: The sheet prints '2' on the lodge: two storeys.

construction.note: Washed pink, the sheet's brick, in its north-west corner; the wash's diagonal run into the glasshouse is read as the colourist's, not the wall's.

parts.from: the sheet's lodge outline, read by hand (T-3164)

draft_plan.note: One rectangle, the whole outline: the sheet draws no wing or bay on it.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED on the draft rules' brick-family values: a hipped roof over two storeys, three bays on its alley front with the door at the south end, one stack, no dormers. Nothing describes the lodge beyond the sheet's '2' and 'D' (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164).
